Sensitivity is 96 dB (1 W/1 m), measured in the operating band. The AMT operating principle uses a folded film diaphragm driven by neodymium magnets to move air with very low moving mass and minimal excursion, resulting in extremely low harmonic distortion and excellent transient accuracy across the high-frequency operating range. The integrated waveguide controls dispersion and provides consistent acoustic loading. Nominal free-air resonance is 2,200 Hz, defining the lower mechanical limit of the driver.

The frequency response rises from approximately 1 kHz, reaching the operating plateau of 94-96 dB in the 4-5 kHz region and remaining flat to beyond 20 kHz. Unlike dome tweeters, the AMT impedance curve shows a very flat response across the audio band (approximately 4 ohms, with minimal variation), reflecting the fundamentally different electrodynamic mechanism. The smooth high-frequency response and very low harmonic distortion above the crossover frequency are characteristic of the AMT topology and distinguish this driver from equivalent dome and compression driver designs.

The driver is rated for 10 W AES into 4 ohms and is suited for high-fidelity and studio monitor applications. A crossover frequency of 2,500-4,000 Hz (18-24 dB/octave high-pass) is recommended, set above the lower mechanical limit to maintain excursion protection and ensure the driver operates in its optimal planar-motion regime. The flat 4-ohm impedance simplifies crossover network design. Good to use with 5-8-inch woofers such as 5FHWX4-380, 8FHWX4-382, 8FHWX4-088, or 8FHMX4-091 in 2-way hi-fi bookshelf, studio monitor, or audiophile-grade loudspeaker designs.
